The suspect should be found not guilty if the jury credits his account, because the statute bars force used to resist arrest but does not bar reasonable force used in self-defense against excessive force by the officer; under the officer's account, the suspect's blow would violate the statute. The note is incorrect: an unlawful arrest does not strip a person of the privilege to use reasonable force against excessive force, and here the arrest appears lawful in any event. The outcome therefore turns on whose version of the facts the jury believes.

CONFIDENCE: 85
